questions.question: Nine years later, the age of B will be equal to the present age of A. Sum of A's age 3 years later and B's age 4 years ago will be 76. If the age of C is half of the present age of B, then what will be C's age (in years) after 10 years?
questions.questionHtml: Nine years later, the age of B will be equal to the present age of A. Sum of A's age 3 years later and B's age 4 years ago will be 76. If the age of C is half of the present age of B, then what will be C's age (in years) after 10 years?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of A be ‘x’

Thus, nine years later B’ s age = x

Therefore, present age of B = (x - 9)

According to question,

Sum of A's age 3 years later and B's age 4 years ago is 76

⇒ (x + 3) + {(x - 9) - 4} = 76

⇒ × = 43

Thus, A’ s present age = 43

B’ s present age = 43 - 9 = 34

Given,

The age of C is half of the present age of B ⇒ C’ s present age = 17

Therefore, C’ s age after 10 years = 17 + 10 = 27.

questions.question: How many types of writs are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.questionHtml: How many types of writs are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 5.

Key Points

  • There are 5 Writz in the Indian Constitution.
  • Article 32  of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
  • It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
  • It is also known as; Right to Constitutional Remedies.
Article Consists of
Article 32

Right to move the Supreme court for the enforcement of fundamental rights including the writs.

  • habeas corpus
  • mandamus
  • prohibition
  • certiorari
  • quo warranto

Additional Information

  • Habeas Corpus: This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained whether in prison or in private custody, before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
  • Mandamus: The writ of command is issued by supreme or high court when any government, court, corporation, or any public authority has to do a public duty but fails to do so.
  • Prohibition: It is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent them from exceeding their jurisdiction.
  • Certiorari: The writ of certiorari can be issued by the supreme or high court for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court, tribunal or quasi-judicial authority.
  • Quo-Warranto: The writ of quo-warranto can be issued by the supreme or high court for asking of by what authority or warrant. It is issued by the court to enquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office.

questions.question: What is the other name of Galileo's law of inertia?
questions.questionHtml: What is the other name of Galileo's law of inertia?
questions.solution:
Option 2 is correct, i.e. Newton's ﬁrst law of motion.

  • The other name of Galileo's law of inertia is Newton's ﬁrst law of motion.
  • Sir Isaac Newton first presented his three laws of motion in 1686.
  • His first law states that every object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change its state by the action of an external force.
  • This concept is generally known as inertia.

Extra information:

  • Newton’s First Law of motion- As per the newton’s first law of motion, if any object is in motion, then it will be continuously in motion, if it is in rest then it will be in rest, till any external force is not applied on it. It is also called the law of inertia.
  • Newton’s Second Law of Motion- The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.
  • Newton’s Third Law of motion- It describes that every action will have an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: Which of the following device is best suited for measuring the temperature inside metallurgical furnaces?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following device is best suited for measuring the temperature inside metallurgical furnaces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pyrometer. 

 

  • Pyrometers are the temperature measuring devices used to detect the object’s temperature and electromagnetic radiation emitted from the object.
  • Principle of Working :
    •  It measures the object’s temperature by sensing the heat/radiation emitted from the object without making contact with the object.
  • It records the temperature level depending upon the intensity of radiation emitted.

  • The pyrometer has two basic components like optical system and detectors that are used to measure the surface temperature of the object. 
  • It is an example of non- contact measurement.
  • Thermocouple is a temperature-measuring device consisting of two wires of different metals joined at each end, and works on Seebeck effect.
  • Thermometer is also an instrument for measuring temperature.
  • A thermistor (or thermal resistor) is defined as a type of resistor whose electrical resistance varies with changes in temperature.

Calculation:

Using Exterior angle property in ΔBDC

⇒ y + 48 = x

From ΔABC,

⇒ ∠ACB = 180 – 2y – ∠A       ......(ii)

From ΔBCD,

⇒ 180 – 2y – ∠A = 180 – y – x – 48

⇒ ∠A = x – y + 48

Using (i)

⇒ ∠A = 48 + 48 = 96o

∴ The value (in degrees) of ∠A is 96°.

cosA = cos2\(A\over2\) - sin2\(A\over2\)

1 + tan2\(A\over2\) = sec2\(A\over2\) = \(1\over cos^2{A\over2}\)

Calculation:

1 + tanA tan\(A\over2\)

⇒ 1 + \({2tan{A\over2}}\over{1-tan^2{A\over2}}\) tan\(A\over2\) 

⇒ 1 + \({2tan^2{A\over2}}\over{1-tan^2{A\over2}}\) = \({1-tan^2{A\over2}+2tan^2{A\over2}}\over{1-tan^2{A\over2}}\)

⇒ \(1\over cosA\) = secA

∴ 1 + tanA tan\(A\over2\) = secA

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. No sooner did I come out of my home to go to the market when it started raining heavily which drenched me completely.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

No sooner did I come out of my home to go to the market when it started raining heavily which drenched me completely.

options.text: No sooner did I come out of my home
options.html: No sooner did I come out of my home
when it started raining heavily
to go to the market
which drenched me completely

questions.solution:
The correct answer is when it started raining heavily

Key Points

  • 'than it started raining heavily' should be there in place of 'when it started raining heavily'
  • If the second event occurs immediately after the first, we can express that idea using the structure no sooner … than.
  • Note that in this structure no sooner introduces the event that occurred first.
    • ​Examples: No sooner had I arrived at the station than the train came.
                               No sooner had we heard the noise than we rushed to the spot.
  • Note that did is also possible in this structure.
    • ​Example: No sooner did I arrive at the station than the train came

Hence, the sentence can be correctly rewritten as: No sooner did I come out of my home to go to market than it started raining heavily which drenched me completely.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P-But he did not know how to find one at that hour. Q-It was his first visit to the city and he didn't know where to go. R-Mohanlal's train was late and it reached Kolkata a little after midnight. S-He thought he would go to a choultry where he would not have to pay rent.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P-But he did not know how to find one at that hour.

Q-It was his first visit to the city and he didn't know where to go.

R-Mohanlal's train was late and it reached Kolkata a little after midnight.

S-He thought he would go to a choultry where he would not have to pay rent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is RQSP.

Key Points

  • R introduces a general, independent idea. P, Q and S cannot be used to start the paragraph as they contain ‘he’, ‘his’ and ‘he’ respectively and only R gives the answer to ‘he’ and ‘his’. Thus, R is the first sentence.
  • Q logically follows R by highlighting his trip to Kolkata that it was his first trip there.
  • After reaching Kolkata for the first time, he wanted to go to a choultry, and thus, sentence S is next in the sequence.
  • Sentence P sums up the entire paragraph and logically follows the previous three sentences.

Hence, the sentence can be correctly rearranged as: Mohanlal's train was late and it reached Kolkata a little after midnight. It was his first visit to the city and he didn't know where to go. He thought he would go to a choultry where he would not have to pay rent. But he did not know how to find one at that hour.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P-And slowly, you reach the pinnacle of self-awareness, experiencing a unity with all life. Q-If you transform your energy positively, it naturally becomes compassion and love. R-Once you experientially are a part of everything then nobody needs to teach you morality. S-Then you can do something to improve the situation, but without anger.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P-And slowly, you reach the pinnacle of self-awareness, experiencing a unity with all life.

Q-If you transform your energy positively, it naturally becomes compassion and love.

R-Once you experientially are a part of everything then nobody needs to teach you morality.

S-Then you can do something to improve the situation, but without anger.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is QPRS. 

Key Points

  • The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble. 
  • The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, or the starting of an incident
  • Part Q will be the first sentence because the sentence 'transforming of energy positively, resulting in compassion and love ' is a universal fact and it is an independent general statement. 
  • Part P mentions the later results of transforming energy positively.
  • R further highlights the fact that when one experiences everything then nobody needs to teach you morality.
  • S concludes the paragraph and logically follows the statements preceding it.


Hence, the sentence can be correctly arranged as: If you transform your energy positively, it naturally becomes compassion and love, and slowly, you reach the pinnacle of self-awareness, experiencing a unity with all life. Once you experientially are a part of everything then nobody needs to teach you morality then you can do something to improve the situation, but without anger.

Hint

  • Once we get the idea that Q is the starting statement, we can mark our answer as option 2 as there is no other option starting from Q.
